Subject: Fee allocation and operator licensing for NovaMed private deployment

Hi Clara —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our call, I wanted to outline two practical packaging options for the private VPC deployment so your procurement team can evaluate the P&L and capital treatment:

Option A — Platform fee + per-site operator license
- Platform fee covers the runtime, orchestration, and observability layer. Priced as an annual entitlement (can be amortized).
- Operator licenses are sold per physical site (up to N GPUs per site) and include access to on-prem operator tooling.

Option B — Platform fee + per-operator-seat license
- Platform fee (lower anchor than A) with operator licenses charged per named seat (SRE/users) which may make sense if you retain a small ops team that manages multiple sites.

Tradeoffs we touched on:
- Amortization: we can offer a 12- or 24-month amortization schedule for the platform fee in the contract.
- Implementation credit: subject to a signed SOW, we can include a one-time implementation credit tied to milestone acceptance.
- Support tiers: Year 1 can include a discounted Tier 2 SRE retainer if you commit 24 months.

I attached a baseline pricing sheet and draft SOW for your finance/procurement review. Could you confirm whether procurement prefers site-based or seat-based operator licensing and whether a 24-month amortization would be required for CAPEX treatment?

Attachments: redwood_privdeploy_pricing_sheet_v1.xlsx; NovaMed_SOW_v2.docx

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if that helps.

—Marcus

Hi Clara —

Thanks for the follow-up and for sending the procurement doc. Quick responses inline below and proposal at the end.

1) "Per-site" map: we define a site as a physical data center location. For your topology that means: Primary DC = Site A; two edge sites = Site B and Site C. Each site license covers up to the agreed GPU band (we can anchor to a band you specify; e.g., up to 8 A100-equivalent GPUs).

2) Amortization minimum: no hard 24-month requirement. We typically offer stronger implementation credits and discounted support retainer rates on 24-month commitments. For a 12-month amortization we can still offer a smaller implementation credit.

Capped operator licenses: yes — we can cap at an agreed headcount or GPU band. Common approach: define a baseline "covered" GPU band and an overage rate per GPU or per-operator seat.

Our recommendation for NovaMed based on the topology in your procurement doc:
- Platform fee: amortize over 24 months (gives you better upfront economics).
- Operator licensing: per-site license for Site A (primary) and 1 pooled seat-per-edge for Site B/C to keep costs predictable.
- Support: Year 1 Tier 2 retainer discounted by 20% if you sign for 24 months.
- Implementation credit: 15% off professional services tied to SOW milestones (pilot acceptance + production cutover).

I've attached an updated pricing sheet that models 12- vs 24-month amortization and both site- and seat-based licensing. If that's acceptable, we'll produce a revised SOW and DocuSign packet.

Attachments: redwood_privdeploy_pricing_sheet_v1.xlsx (updated)

Next steps: please confirm the licensing approach (site vs seat) and whether you want us to model a capped GPU band. Once confirmed, Kimberly and Marissa will finalize the commercial worksheet and SOW language.

Best,
—Marcus

Marcus / Marissa —

Quick internal note on margins and guardrails before we send a final proposal:

- If we go 24-month amortization + 15% implementation credit + 20% support discount, our blended margin tightens. Recommend we protect gross margin by adding either a contractually capped annual platform fee increase (e.g., CPI + 3%) or by moving to a small consumption overage (per GPU-hour) for burst usage.

- Operator license cap: agree to capped GPU band but add a quarterly reconciliation clause so we don't underprice sustained growth.

- For SOW milestones: tie the 15% implementation credit to (1) pilot sign-off and (2) production acceptance. If pilot fails we revert to 10% and have an engineering change order path.

I'll draft the commercial worksheet and alternative language for the SOW. Marcus — once Clara confirms site vs seat we can finalize numbers.

-Kim
